- [x] I agree to license this contribution under the terms of [LICENSE.txt](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/LICENSE.txt).
- [x] I ran `pre-commit run` and committed any formatting changes.
- [x] I reviewed the Hard Rules in the `AGENTS.md` for each directory this PR touches (see [root AGENTS.md § Reviewing a PR](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/AGENTS.md#reviewing-a-pr-human-or-agent)) and my changes comply.
- [ ] I added GitHub labels: one `cat-*`, one or more `area:*` / `op:*`, and one `orig-*` (see [label list](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/labels)).

Maintainer action: apply the agreed labels `cat-feature`, `mod-frontend`, and `mod-backend`. The author account cannot apply upstream labels.

## Affected area

C++ frontend graph API, Python API and bindings, documentation, samples, and tests.

## Summary

- Add application-defined reduction graphs with typed identities and reducer callbacks.
- Expose custom-reduction helpers and reduction modifiers in C++ and Python.
- Add argmax, argmin and sampling examples, supported HLO-derived argmax regressions, plan round trips, and input-validation coverage.

## Reviewer overview

Start with [How custom reductions work](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/2218/files?short_path=7f98261#diff-7f982619e548086ecf52f241ff5265416e8462452769907876050e5e114311be) for the concepts, data flow and an argmax example. This Markdown guide is an added file in this PR (`docs/operations/custom_reduction/overview.md`) and will merge with the feature. It is also listed under **Custom Reduction → How custom reductions work** in the documentation navigation.

A reduction can carry several streams as one state: argmax carries a `(value, index)` pair and combines both according to an explicit tie/NaN rule. The reducer callback builds a symbolic scalar graph during operation-graph construction. cuDNN then executes the resulting reduction through the normal execution-plan path.

<details>
<summary>Suggested review order</summary>

1. **Public contract:** `Custom_reduction_identity` and `Custom_reduction_attributes::set_reducer` in [graph_properties.h](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/2218/files#diff-8de4ebae84d65a0e2232d6b8c224d81b93141f455a4d5b1184b0f409775ddc14), followed by the [reduction modifiers](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/2218/files#diff-03ea80d1b60dcd8630e8a0485103f6adb0c268c71e09c828ee23d056e0e81a30).
2. **Construction and lowering:** `INode::custom_reduction` and node validation in [custom_reduction.h](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/2218/files#diff-27e46df57322b364cd9af2d0f638f8728df8d55f87d31abe4147cf8e7b59cb34), then `CustomReductionNode::expand_node`, `validate_reducer_body` and `create_cudnn_operations` in [graph_interface.h](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/2218/files#diff-6c65ad35b83a1ae7201fd8832e49381b63d2dbc95cdd55ed8120b434e05723cf).
3. **Python integration:** `_custom_reduction_callback` and stream lowering in [_pygraph.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/2218/files#diff-e420bdcb05ffced536ff2413c889ed3e4222c141025f4b602ed9179c1e6705ee), plus `PyGraph::custom_reduction` and callback ownership in [the native binding](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/2218/files#diff-2fa21d8734faa7314e33700268ee5b229f2a94788bb8a9481ca64e52f5376a4c).
4. **Serialization and bindings:** [plan_metadata.h](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/2218/files#diff-0df0b6273d36b23278be07ed99e5fb5bdaf81ef81c17b79df83afa1a7fbd1835) carries typed scalars and validates owned-buffer metadata used by plan round trips and replay.
5. **Regression examples:** [literal XLA HLO reductions](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/2218/files#diff-e17f67a18b47f95df678891f26119ad852bfa41028d4ac7308e6386ba17d68ff) and [Python custom-reduction tests](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/2218/files#diff-88f7de044c633a510db0c529d00c6a7981133541872b29a07390d48168e39dfa), alongside the samples linked in the API reference.

</details>

## Python sample

The [custom-reduction argmax notebook](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/pull/2218/files?short_path=c589cca#diff-c589cca39a45fcd93504a838db2b5e44d6324c9eb1a6bff1c4f3426897d5dc79) is included in this PR at `samples/python/71_custom_reduction_argmax.ipynb`, following the repository's numbered Python tutorial convention and listed in `samples/README.md`.

It walks through greedy decoding, argmax/argmin NaN rules, speculative-decoding verification, masked argmax, and Gumbel-max sampling, with PyTorch reference checks. All seven code cells passed in the local cuDNN 9.29 / SM100 qualification run.

## Why

Let graph callers express custom reduction behavior through a consistent C++ and Python interface.

## Related issues

None.

## API and compatibility impact

Additive C++ and Python graph APIs.

## Testing

Local execution with cuDNN 9.29 on SM100:

- `bin/tests`: 148 passed, 3 skipped; 134827 assertions passed.
- `bin/samples "[custom_reduction]"`: 18 passed; 3509 assertions. Separate `"[custom_reduction_argmax_all_shapes]"` run: 1 passed; 15120 assertions across 105 shape/type groups.
- `python3 -m pytest test_custom_reduction.py`: 50 passed, 1 skipped. Adjacent serialization, plan and existing-reduction controls: 24 passed.
- `71_custom_reduction_argmax.ipynb`: all 7 code cells passed.

Compatibility and quality checks:

- Actual cuDNN 9.26 headers with JSON and FE exceptions disabled: module build and C++17/Werror HLO syntax checks passed; 2 API/refusal tests passed on the 9.26 runtime.
- Targeted failure/restoration checks completed for all 149 new test declarations.
- Pinned clang-format, Black, Black Jupyter and SPDX hooks passed with `pre-commit run --all-files` in an isolated clean worktree.

```text
@cudnn-ci-bot run backend,pycudnn,python/misc,python_samples,python/conv,python/sdpa/misc
```

+# Custom Reduction
+
+For a conceptual walkthrough, see How custom reductions work ([docs](/operations/CustomReduction/overview), [GitHub](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/docs/operations/custom_reduction/overview.md)).
+
+A custom reduction reduces one or more input tensors along the same dimensions. Each input is a stream. A reducer callback that you write sets how two values of a stream combine. The callback can read the values of all streams, so a reduction such as argmax (a value stream and an index stream) is one operation.
+
+The frontend calls the reducer when it builds the operation graph. After an expansion that succeeds, the frontend keeps the child graph and does not call the reducer again. If the reducer throws an exception, the build returns `INVALID_VALUE` with the exception message (Python: a `RuntimeError` that contains the type and the message of the Python exception). If the reducer throws an exception or the frontend refuses the child graph, the frontend does not keep the child graph, and the next build calls the reducer again. The reducer adds pointwise operations to a child graph. cuDNN runs that child graph for each combination step.
+
+## Requirements
+
+The operation needs cuDNN 9.29.0 or later. The API is always present. With an older cuDNN, building the operation graph returns `GRAPH_NOT_SUPPORTED` with the message "Custom reduction requires cuDNN v9.29.0" (Python: `cudnn.cudnnGraphNotSupportedError`). The frontend reads the version of the loaded cuDNN library before it calls the reducer, so with an older library the reducer does not run. This is also true for a program that you compile with cuDNN 9.29 headers and run with an older library.
+
+## Semantics
+
+- Stream `i` has the input `X[i]` and the output `Y[i]`. All inputs have the same shape.
+- `Y[i]` has the shape of `X[i]`, with extent 1 in each reduced dimension. `Y[i]` has the data type of `X[i]`.
+- The reducer gets the child graph and two lists, `lhs` and `rhs`, with one scalar tensor for each stream. It returns one scalar tensor for each stream.
+- The reducer body contains only pointwise operations. A build of the body gives `GRAPH_NOT_SUPPORTED` for any other operation before an operation in the body expands, also if the reducer builds the child graph itself, on any thread. Thus a custom reduction or an SDPA `score_mod` in the body never runs. A reducer can build a different graph that contains a custom reduction. Do not assign to or copy the child graph object. An operand is `lhs`, `rhs`, the result of a body operation, or a compile-time constant.
+- The combination must be associative and commutative.
+- The identity of stream `i` must be a two-sided identity of the combination. For example, use 0 for a sum and -inf for a maximum.
+- The identity has exactly the data type of `Y[i]`. The frontend does not convert identities.
+- The compute type of a stream is the data type of the body values of that stream. If you do not set it, the stream computes in its own data type. A compute type must be an integer type for an integer or boolean stream, and a floating-point type for a floating-point stream.
+- The semantic key identifies the reducer in the graph key. Change the key when the behavior of the reducer changes.
+- The graph JSON shows a custom reduction for inspection only. A graph with a custom reduction cannot be deserialized; deserialize the execution plan instead.
+
+## C++ API
+
+```cpp
+std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Tensor_attributes>>
+custom_reduction(std::vector<std::shared_ptr<Tensor_attributes>> inputs, Custom_reduction_attributes attributes);
+```
+
+The function returns one output tensor for each input, in input order.
+
+`Custom_reduction_attributes` setters:
+
+```cpp
+using Reducer_t = std::function<std::vector<Tensor_t>(Graph_t graph, std::vector<Tensor_t> lhs, std::vector<Tensor_t> rhs)>;
+
+Custom_reduction_attributes&
+set_reducer(Reducer_t reducer, std::string semantic_key);
+
+Custom_reduction_attributes&
+set_reduction_dims(std::vector<int64_t> dims);  // strictly ascending
+
+Custom_reduction_attributes&
+set_identity_values(std::vector<Custom_reduction_identity> identities);  // one for each stream
+
+Custom_reduction_attributes&
+set_compute_data_types(std::vector<DataType_t> types);  // one for each stream
+
+Custom_reduction_attributes&
+set_compute_data_type(DataType_t type);  // the same type for each stream
+
+Custom_reduction_attributes&
+set_name(std::string const&);
+```
+
+`set_compute_data_types` and `set_compute_data_type` replace each other. The last call sets the compute types.
+
+`Custom_reduction_identity` holds one identity value and its exact data type. Make it from a value of the stream type:
+
+| Data type | Constructor argument |
+|---|---|
+| `INT8`, `UINT8`, `INT32`, `UINT32`, `INT64` | `int8_t`, `uint8_t`, `int32_t`, `uint32_t`, `int64_t` |
+| `FLOAT`, `DOUBLE` | `float`, `double` |
+| `HALF`, `BFLOAT16` | `half`, `nv_bfloat16` |
+| `FP8_E4M3`, `FP8_E5M2` | `Custom_reduction_fp8_e4m3{bits}`, `Custom_reduction_fp8_e5m2{bits}` |
+| `BYTE_BOOLEAN` | `Custom_reduction_byte_boolean{byte}` (0 is false; each other value is true) |
+
+`cudnn_frontend::graph::reduction_modifiers::sum`, `max` and `min` take a `Custom_reduction_attributes` and return it with a single-stream reducer and its semantic key. They do not set an identity or a compute type.
+
+`reduction_modifiers` also has argmax and argmin. These set the reducer, the semantic key and the identities. They do not set a compute type.
+
+```cpp
+enum class Arg_nan_rule { TORCH, XLA, IGNORE_NAN };
+
+Custom_reduction_attributes
+argmax(Custom_reduction_attributes attributes,
+       DataType_t value_type,                      // the data type of the value stream
+       DataType_t index_type = DataType_t::INT32,  // the data type of the index stream
+       Arg_nan_rule rule     = Arg_nan_rule::TORCH);
+
+Custom_reduction_attributes
+argmin(Custom_reduction_attributes attributes,
+       DataType_t value_type,
+       DataType_t index_type = DataType_t::INT32,
+       Arg_nan_rule rule     = Arg_nan_rule::TORCH);
+```
+
+- `argmax` and `argmin` reduce two streams: stream 0 holds the values and stream 1 holds the index of each element along the reduced dimensions (for example 0 to N−1), in a tensor of the full input shape. Among equal values, the lowest index value wins.
+- `value_type` and `index_type` are the data types of the two streams; the identities have exactly these types. A value stream that is not `FLOAT`, `HALF`, `BFLOAT16` or `DOUBLE`, or an index stream that is not `INT32` or `INT64`, gives `INVALID_VALUE` from `validate`.
+- The identities are `(-inf, largest index)` for argmax and `(+inf, largest index)` for argmin, and `(NaN, largest index)` for `IGNORE_NAN`, where the largest index is the maximum of the index type. Each is a two-sided identity of its body for any index values smaller than the largest index.
+- The frontend builds the graph for each stream type; the cuDNN library decides which stream types and body forms it runs, and this can change with the library version. If the library does not support the graph, the build returns its status unchanged (`GRAPH_NOT_SUPPORTED` for a not-supported status).
+
+The rule sets the result for NaN values. Each rule gives the lowest index among equal values, and `-0` equals `+0`.
+
+| Rule | Row with NaN values | Commutative | Matches |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `TORCH` (default) | the first NaN | yes | `torch.argmax`, `torch.argmin` |
+| `XLA` | one of the NaN positions; with more than one NaN, which one is not specified | no, for two NaN values | the XLA argmax and argmin comparators |
+| `IGNORE_NAN` | the best number; a row of NaN only gives its first position | yes | a NaN-ignoring argmax or argmin |
+
+The backend contract requires a commutative combination. The `XLA` body is not commutative for two NaN values, so for those rows its result depends on the reduction order.
+
+Example, an argmax over dimension 1 of BF16 values:
+
+```cpp
+auto outputs = graph.custom_reduction(
+    {values, indices},
+    reduction_modifiers::argmax(Custom_reduction_attributes().set_name("argmax").set_reduction_dims({1}),
+                                DataType_t::BFLOAT16));
+outputs[1]->set_output(true);  // the index
+```
+
+Example, a sum over dimension 1:
+
+```cpp
+auto Y = graph.custom_reduction({X},
+                                reduction_modifiers::sum(Custom_reduction_attributes()
+                                                             .set_name("row_sum")
+                                                             .set_reduction_dims({1})
+                                                             .set_identity_values({Custom_reduction_identity(0.0f)})))[0];
+Y->set_output(true);
+```
+
+Example, a reducer that writes the body:
+
+```cpp
+auto reducer = [](Custom_reduction_attributes::Graph_t body,
+                  std::vector<Custom_reduction_attributes::Tensor_t> lhs,
+                  std::vector<Custom_reduction_attributes::Tensor_t> rhs) {
+    auto larger = body->pointwise(
+        lhs[0], rhs[0], Pointwise_attributes().set_mode(PointwiseMode_t::MAX).set_compute_data_type(DataType_t::FLOAT));
+    return std::vector<Custom_reduction_attributes::Tensor_t>{larger};
+};
+auto Y = graph.custom_reduction({X},
+                                Custom_reduction_attributes()
+                                    .set_reducer(reducer, "my_project.row_max.v1")
+                                    .set_reduction_dims({1})
+                                    .set_identity_values({Custom_reduction_identity(-INFINITY)}))[0];
+```
+
+## Python API
+
+- `pygraph.custom_reduction(inputs, reducer, reducer_semantic_key, reduction_dims, identity_values, *, compute_data_types=None, compute_data_type=None, name="")`
+  - **inputs**: list of input tensors, one for each stream.
+  - **reducer**: callable `reducer(graph, lhs, rhs)` that returns a list with one tensor for each stream. The reducer can capture parent tensors, use them as operands and return them. It can read captured parent graph state; add reducer operations to the provided child graph.
+  - **reducer_semantic_key**: string that identifies the reducer in the graph key.
+  - **reduction_dims**: list of reduced dimensions, strictly ascending.
+  - **identity_values**: list of `cudnn.custom_reduction_identity`, one for each stream.
+  - **compute_data_types**: optional list with one `cudnn.data_type` for each stream.
+  - **compute_data_type**: optional `cudnn.data_type` for each stream. Give `compute_data_types` or `compute_data_type`, not both.
+  - Returns the list of output tensors.
+- `cudnn.custom_reduction_identity(dtype, value)` makes an identity from a Python value. Use a real number (`numbers.Real`, for example a `float` or a NumPy floating-point scalar) for `FLOAT` and `DOUBLE`, and an integer (`numbers.Integral`) for the integer types. A `bool` is not a number for these types. The value must have an exact representation in `dtype`. Use a `bool` for `BYTE_BOOLEAN`. Use `float("inf")` and `float("-inf")` for infinite identities.
+- `cudnn.custom_reduction_identity.from_bits(dtype, bits)` makes an identity from its exact storage bits. Use it for `HALF`, `BFLOAT16`, FP8 and NaN encodings.
+- `cudnn.reduction_modifiers.sum()`, `max()` and `min()` return a dictionary with the `reducer` and `reducer_semantic_key` arguments. These are the C++ `reduction_modifiers` reducers and keys.

+# How custom reductions work
+
+A custom reduction lets an application describe the combining step as a small graph. Its state contains one or more tensor streams. Each stream is one component of the reduction state. For example, argmax carries both a candidate value and its index, allowing the comparison to update them together. The operation fits into the ordinary graph, so its streams can come from graph inputs or preceding operations, and its outputs can feed later operations.
+
+## What the caller provides
+
+The caller supplies input tensors, reduction dimensions, one typed identity per stream, a reducer callback and a semantic key. Optional compute types control the scalar arithmetic for each stream. All streams share a shape; the operation returns an output for each stream in the same order, preserving rank with extent one on reduced dimensions.
+
+`Custom_reduction_identity` owns the scalar value and its exact type and storage representation. Its type must match the corresponding output stream. This keeps identities such as floating-point negative infinity and an integer index sentinel distinct. For order-independent results, the caller supplies an associative, commutative combination and matching two-sided identities.
+
+## Graph construction and execution
+
+Calling `custom_reduction` records a frontend node and creates output tensors. During expansion, the frontend creates a candidate child graph containing symbolic scalar `lhs` and `rhs` tensors for each stream. It invokes `reducer(child_graph, lhs, rhs)` to build the pointwise combination and return one resulting scalar tensor per stream. These tensors describe the state transition; the callback runs on the host during graph construction.
+
+Validation checks the stream metadata, identities, output shapes, reducer operands and scalar body boundaries. The frontend retains the child graph after its expansion and body validation succeed. A callback exception or refused candidate body leaves that candidate uncommitted, allowing a later expansion to try again. Rebuilding an already materialized node reuses its child graph.
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart LR
+    A[Streams, axes, identities, reducer and key] --> B[Frontend node and outputs]
+    B --> C[Build scalar reducer child graph]
+    C --> D[Backend reduction descriptor and plan]
+    D --> E[GPU execution and replay]
+```
+
+The backend bridge builds the child operation graph and attaches it to a cuDNN reduction operation. It supplies input/output descriptors, reduction dimensions, typed identity values, and the child graph's `lhs`, `rhs` and result UIDs. Compute types are forwarded when explicitly supplied. The resulting parent graph follows the normal plan-selection and execution path. Execution binds tensor buffers and workspace to that plan; repeated execution runs the emitted reduction without re-entering the reducer callback.
+
+## Keys, captured state and Python ownership
+
+The semantic key identifies reducer behavior in the graph key. It must be deterministic and change whenever callback logic or captured configuration changes the generated body. Captured configuration becomes part of graph construction; changing execution input buffers supplies new data to the existing plan.
+
+Python records custom reductions in its graph IR, then lowers ordered streams, identities, attributes and outputs into the C++ graph. Its callback adapter also resolves captured parent tensor operands and returned tensors through the lowering map. The native wrapper retains callback state, gives the child proxy shared ownership, and exposes callback references to Python's cyclic garbage collector. This supports captured parent state and retained child proxies without losing callbacks or hiding reference cycles. Child graph construction belongs inside the callback; a retained proxy should not be used to edit the materialized reducer afterward.
+
+Graph JSON records inspection structure and the semantic key. Execution-plan serialization preserves the built backend plan; rebuilding a reducer from graph JSON would require the original callable, which is not serialized.
+
+## Argmax as a state transition
+
+Supply a value tensor and an equally shaped tensor of index values. The argmax helper builds comparisons and selects that carry the winning `(value, index)` pair together, including its tie and NaN policy. Its default identities are typed negative infinity and the largest index value. The caller chooses which result to expose:
+
+```python
+value, index = graph.custom_reduction(
+    [values, indices], reduction_dims=[1],
+    **cudnn.reduction_modifiers.argmax(cudnn.data_type.FLOAT),
+)
+index.set_output(True)
+```
+
+See the Custom Reduction API reference ([docs](/operations/CustomReduction), [GitHub](https://github.com/NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend/blob/develop/docs/operations/CustomReduction.md)) for signatures and examples.

+Each function returns keyword arguments of ``custom_reduction``; pass them with ``**``.
+The semantic keys are the keys of the C++ ``cudnn_frontend::graph::reduction_modifiers``.

+- ``argmax`` and ``argmin`` (a value stream and an index stream that holds the position of each

+class ArgNanRule(enum.Enum):
+    """How ``argmax`` and ``argmin`` order NaN.
+
+    Each rule gives the lowest index among equal values, and -0 equals +0.
+
+    - ``TORCH``: NaN is above every number for argmax and below every number for argmin, so
+      the first NaN wins (``torch.argmax``, ``torch.argmin``).
+    - ``XLA``: the XLA comparator. A NaN wins, but it is not commutative for two NaN values, so
+      when a row holds more than one NaN the result is one of the NaN positions, not specified which.
+    - ``IGNORE_NAN``: a NaN loses to every number; a row of NaN only gives its first position.
+    """

+    XLA = "xla"
+    IGNORE_NAN = "ignore_nan"

+def _single_stream(method, name, semantic_key):
+    def reducer(graph, lhs, rhs):
+        compute_type = lhs[0].get_data_type()
+        result = getattr(graph, method)(lhs[0], rhs[0], compute_data_type=compute_type, name=name)
+        result.set_data_type(compute_type)
+        return [result]
+
+    return {"reducer": reducer, "reducer_semantic_key": semantic_key}
+
+
+def sum():
+    """Reducer arguments for ``lhs + rhs``."""
+    return _single_stream("add", "reduction_modifiers::sum", "cudnn_frontend.reduction_modifiers.sum.v1")
+

+def max():
+    """Reducer arguments for ``max(lhs, rhs)``."""
+    return _single_stream("max", "reduction_modifiers::max", "cudnn_frontend.reduction_modifiers.max.v1")
+
+
+def min():
+    """Reducer arguments for ``min(lhs, rhs)``."""
+    return _single_stream("min", "reduction_modifiers::min", "cudnn_frontend.reduction_modifiers.min.v1")
+

+    result = getattr(graph, method)(*operands, compute_data_type=compute_type, name=name)
+    result.set_data_type(result_type)
+    return result
+
+

+# logical modes and the select of two predicates read one-bit operands, so they use the index type.
+def _arg_reducer(is_max, rule):
+    better = "cmp_gt" if is_max else "cmp_lt"
+    better_or_equal = "cmp_ge" if is_max else "cmp_le"
+    worse_or_equal = "cmp_le" if is_max else "cmp_ge"
+
+    def reducer(graph, lhs, rhs):
+        B = data_type.BOOLEAN
+        T = lhs[0].get_data_type()
+        I = lhs[1].get_data_type()
+        vl, il = lhs[0], lhs[1]
+        vr, ir = rhs[0], rhs[1]
+

+            nan_l = _op(graph, "cmp_neq", "nan_l", T, B, vl, vl)
+            keep_vl = _op(graph, "logical_or", "keep_value_l", I, B, better_l, nan_l)
+            value = _op(graph, "binary_select", "value", T, T, vl, vr, keep_vl)
+            equal = _op(graph, "cmp_eq", "equal", T, B, vl, vr)

+            tie = _op(graph, "logical_and", "tie_to_l", I, B, equal, lower)
+            keep_il = _op(graph, "logical_or", "keep_index_l", I, B, keep_vl, tie)
+            index = _op(graph, "binary_select", "index", I, I, il, ir, keep_il)
+            return [value, index]

+        # The lhs wins on win_if_lower when its index is the lower one, else on win_if_higher.
+        lower = _op(graph, "cmp_lt", "lower", I, B, il, ir)

+            at_l = _op(graph, better_or_equal, "better_or_equal", T, B, vl, vr)
+            win_if_lower = _op(graph, "logical_or", "win_if_lower", I, B, nan_l, at_l)
+            # No compare mode is unordered, so "better or unordered" is NOT(worse or equal).
+            not_better = _op(graph, worse_or_equal, "worse_or_equal", T, B, vl, vr)

+            number_r = _op(graph, "cmp_eq", "number_r", T, B, vr, vr)

+        else:

+            nan_r = _op(graph, "cmp_neq", "nan_r", T, B, vr, vr)
+            win_if_lower = _op(graph, "logical_or", "win_if_lower", I, B, at_l, nan_r)
+            better_l = _op(graph, better, "better", T, B, vl, vr)
+            number_l = _op(graph, "cmp_eq", "number_l", T, B, vl, vl)
+            only_r_nan = _op(graph, "logical_and", "only_r_nan", I, B, nan_r, number_l)
+            win_if_higher = _op(graph, "logical_or", "win_if_higher", I, B, better_l, only_r_nan)

+        index = _op(graph, "binary_select", "index", I, I, il, ir, keep_l)
+        value = _op(graph, "binary_select", "value", T, T, vl, vr, keep_l)

+
+    return reducer
+
+
+# Bits of (-inf, +inf, quiet NaN). Any other value type gets FLOAT bits, so the graph refuses a value stream that is
+# not floating point.
+_FLOAT_SPECIAL_BITS = {
+    data_type.HALF: (0xFC00, 0x7C00, 0x7E00),
+    data_type.BFLOAT16: (0xFF80, 0x7F80, 0x7FC0),
+    data_type.FLOAT: (0xFF800000, 0x7F800000, 0x7FC00000),
+    data_type.DOUBLE: (0xFFF0000000000000, 0x7FF0000000000000, 0x7FF8000000000000),
+}
+_NEGATIVE_INFINITY, _POSITIVE_INFINITY, _QUIET_NAN = range(3)
+
+
+def _rule(rule):
+    if isinstance(rule, ArgNanRule):
+        return rule
+    try:
+        return ArgNanRule(rule)
+    except ValueError:
+        raise ValueError(f"rule must be an ArgNanRule or one of 'torch', 'xla', 'ignore_nan'; got {rule!r}") from None
+
+
+def _arg_modifier(is_max, value_type, index_type, rule):
+    rule = _rule(rule)
+    kind = "argmax" if is_max else "argmin"
+    # The largest index loses every tie, so the identity is two-sided for any index values. Under IGNORE_NAN a NaN
+    # loses to every number, so the infinity identity would win against a NaN element; (NaN, largest index) does not.
+    special = _QUIET_NAN if rule is ArgNanRule.IGNORE_NAN else (_NEGATIVE_INFINITY if is_max else _POSITIVE_INFINITY)
+    value_dtype = value_type if value_type in _FLOAT_SPECIAL_BITS else data_type.FLOAT
+    # Any index type other than INT64 gets an INT32 identity, so the graph refuses any other index stream type.
+    index_dtype = data_type.INT64 if index_type == data_type.INT64 else data_type.INT32

+    return {
+        "reducer": _arg_reducer(is_max, rule),
+        "reducer_semantic_key": f"cudnn_frontend.reduction_modifiers.{kind}.{rule.value}.v1",
+        "identity_values": [
+            custom_reduction_identity.from_bits(value_dtype, _FLOAT_SPECIAL_BITS[value_dtype][special]),
+            custom_reduction_identity(index_dtype, largest_index),
+        ],
+    }
+
+
+def argmax(value_type, index_type=data_type.INT32, rule=ArgNanRule.TORCH):
+    """Reducer arguments for the argmax of a (value, index) pair of streams.

+    ``value_type`` and ``index_type`` are the data types of the two streams. ``rule`` is an
+    ``ArgNanRule`` or its value (``"torch"``, ``"xla"`` or ``"ignore_nan"``). The identities are
+    (-inf, largest index), or (NaN, largest index) for ``IGNORE_NAN``.
+    """
+    return _arg_modifier(True, value_type, index_type, rule)
+
+
+def argmin(value_type, index_type=data_type.INT32, rule=ArgNanRule.TORCH):
+    """Reducer arguments for the argmin of a (value, index) pair of streams; see ``argmax``.
+
+    The identities are (+inf, largest index), or (NaN, largest index) for ``IGNORE_NAN``.
+    """
+    return _arg_modifier(False, value_type, index_type, rule)

+class _BodyValue:
+    def __init__(self, name):
+        self.name = name
+        self.data_type = None
+
+    def set_data_type(self, data_type):
+        self.data_type = data_type

+    def get_data_type(self):
+        return self.data_type

+class _RecordingBody:
+    """Records the operations that a reducer adds, in order, for a host model of the body."""
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.operations = []
+
+    def __getattr__(self, method):
+        def operation(*operands, compute_data_type, name):
+            result = _BodyValue(str(len(self.operations)))
+            self.operations.append((method, operands, compute_data_type, result))
+            return result
+
+        return operation
+
+
+# The body operations as the reducer body evaluates them: ordered compares are false on NaN, CMP_NEQ is unordered.
+_BODY_SEMANTICS = {
+    "cmp_gt": lambda a, b: a > b,
+    "cmp_ge": lambda a, b: a >= b,
+    "cmp_lt": lambda a, b: a < b,
+    "cmp_le": lambda a, b: a <= b,
+    "cmp_eq": lambda a, b: a == b,
+    "cmp_neq": lambda a, b: not (a == b),
+    "logical_and": lambda a, b: a and b,
+    "logical_or": lambda a, b: a or b,
+    "logical_not": lambda a: not a,
+    "binary_select": lambda x, b, t: x if t else b,
+}
+
+
+def _record_arg_body(arguments, value_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT):
+    body = _RecordingBody()
+    lhs = [_BodyValue("vl").set_data_type(value_type), _BodyValue("il").set_data_type(cudnn.data_type.INT32)]
+    rhs = [_BodyValue("vr").set_data_type(value_type), _BodyValue("ir").set_data_type(cudnn.data_type.INT32)]
+    results = arguments["reducer"](body, lhs, rhs)
+    return body.operations, lhs, rhs, results

+def _identity_float(identity):
+    import struct
+
+    return struct.unpack(">f", bytes.fromhex(identity.raw_hex))[0]
+
+
+def _model_combine(operations, lhs, rhs, results):
+    def combine(left, right):
+        env = {id(lhs[0]): left[0], id(lhs[1]): left[1], id(rhs[0]): right[0], id(rhs[1]): right[1]}
+        for method, operands, _, result in operations:
+            env[id(result)] = _BODY_SEMANTICS[method](*(env[id(operand)] for operand in operands))
+        return env[id(results[0])], env[id(results[1])]
+
+    return combine
+
+
+def _host_arg_index(values, is_max, rule):
+    import math
+
+    nan_positions = [i for i, v in enumerate(values) if math.isnan(v)]
+    numbers = [v for v in values if not math.isnan(v)]
+    if rule in ("torch", "xla") and nan_positions:
+        return set(nan_positions) if rule == "xla" else {nan_positions[0]}
+    if not numbers:
+        return {0}
+    best = max(numbers) if is_max else min(numbers)
+    return {next(i for i, v in enumerate(values) if v == best)}
+

+def _fold_mismatches(combine, identity, is_max, rule, reference_rule):
+    import itertools
+
+    specials = [float("nan"), float("inf"), float("-inf"), 3.0, 1.0, 0.0, -0.0, 1e-40]
+    mismatches = folds = 0
+    for length in (1, 2, 3):
+        for values in itertools.product(specials, repeat=length):
+            accepted = _host_arg_index(values, is_max, reference_rule)
+            for order in itertools.permutations(range(length)):
+                for sides in itertools.product((False, True), repeat=length):
+                    accumulator = identity
+                    for position, element_left in zip(order, sides):
+                        element = (values[position], position)
+                        accumulator = combine(element, accumulator) if element_left else combine(accumulator, element)
+                    folds += 1
+                    mismatches += accumulator[1] not in accepted
+    return mismatches, folds

+            ("binary_select", ("vl", "vr", "2")),

+        ("binary_select", ("il", "ir", "8")),

+    if cudnn_handle is None:
+        pytest.skip("cuDNN backend is unavailable")

+_TORCH_TO_CUDNN = {
+    "float32": cudnn.data_type.FLOAT,
+    "bfloat16": cudnn.data_type.BFLOAT16,
+    "float16": cudnn.data_type.HALF,
+    "float64": cudnn.data_type.DOUBLE,

+def _arg_graph(cudnn_handle, torch, x, index_type, kind, rule, output="index"):
+    value_type = _TORCH_TO_CUDNN[str(x.dtype).split(".")[-1]]
+    graph = cudnn.pygraph(
+        handle=cudnn_handle,
+        io_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT,
+        intermediate_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT,
+        compute_data_type=cudnn.data_type.FLOAT,
+    )
+    x_t = graph.tensor(dim=list(x.shape), stride=list(x.stride()), data_type=value_type, name="X")
+    idx_t = graph.tensor(dim=list(x.shape), stride=list(x.stride()), data_type=index_type, name="IDX")
+    value, index = graph.custom_reduction(
+        [x_t, idx_t], reduction_dims=[1], name=f"{kind}_{rule}", **getattr(cudnn.reduction_modifiers, kind)(value_type, index_type, rule)
+    )
+    (index if output == "index" else value).set_output(True)
+    return graph, x_t, idx_t, value, index

+def _run_arg(cudnn_handle, torch, x, kind, rule):
+    graph, x_t, idx_t, _, index = _arg_graph(cudnn_handle, torch, x, cudnn.data_type.INT32, kind, rule)
+    graph.build([cudnn.heur_mode.A])
+    rows, extent = x.shape
+    iota = torch.arange(extent, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda").expand(rows, extent).contiguous()
+    out = torch.full((rows, 1), -7, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    workspace = torch.empty(graph.get_workspace_size(), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    graph.execute({x_t: x, idx_t: iota, index: out}, workspace, handle=cudnn_handle)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return out.view(-1).long()

+def _arg_check(torch, x, got, kind, rule):
+    """Number of rows whose index breaks the rule: torch.argmax / argmin for TORCH, any NaN position of a row with NaN
+    for XLA, the first best number (the first position for a row of NaN only) for IGNORE_NAN."""
+    is_max = kind == "argmax"
+    rows = torch.arange(x.shape[0], device=x.device)
+    in_range = (got >= 0) & (got < x.shape[1])
+    if not bool(in_range.all()):
+        return int((~in_range).sum())
+    if rule == "torch":
+        want = torch.argmax(x, dim=1) if is_max else torch.argmin(x, dim=1)
+        return int((got != want).sum())
+    xf = x.float()
+    nan = torch.isnan(xf)
+    numbers = xf.masked_fill(nan, float("-inf") if is_max else float("inf"))
+    best = numbers.amax(dim=1, keepdim=True) if is_max else numbers.amin(dim=1, keepdim=True)
+    first_best = torch.argmax(((numbers == best) & ~nan).to(torch.uint8), dim=1)
+    has_number = (~nan).any(dim=1)
+    if rule == "xla":
+        has_nan = nan.any(dim=1)
+        ok = torch.where(has_nan, nan[rows, got], got == first_best)
+    else:
+        ok = got == torch.where(has_number, first_best, torch.zeros_like(first_best))
+    return int((~ok).sum())

+def _arg_parity_rows(torch, dtype, extent):
+    """Rows of the NaN, tie, signed zero, infinity and subnormal classes, then random rows."""
+    nan, inf = float("nan"), float("inf")
+    tiny = torch.finfo(dtype).tiny if dtype != torch.float32 else 1e-40
+    rows = []
+
+    def row(**positions):
+        r = torch.randn(extent, dtype=torch.float32) * 3
+        for position, value in positions.items():
+            r[int(position[1:])] = value
+        return r
+
+    last = extent - 1
+    rows += [row(), row(p3=50.0, p9=50.0), row(p5=nan), row(p0=nan, **{f"p{last}": nan}), row(p4=nan, p5=nan)]
+    rows += [row(p7=inf, p2=nan), row(p2=inf, p7=nan), row(p1=inf, p6=inf), row(p1=-inf, p6=-inf)]
+    zeros = -torch.rand(extent) - 1
+    for first, second in ((0.0, -0.0), (-0.0, 0.0)):
+        r = zeros.clone()
+        r[3], r[8] = first, second
+        rows.append(r)
+    rows.append(torch.full((extent,), -inf))
+    rows.append(torch.full((extent,), inf))
+    all_nan = torch.full((extent,), nan)
+    all_nan[1::2] = -nan
+    rows.append(all_nan)
+    neginf_nan = torch.full((extent,), -inf)
+    neginf_nan[0] = nan
+    rows.append(neginf_nan)
+    sub = torch.full((extent,), -inf)
+    sub[4], sub[9] = tiny / 2, tiny / 4
+    rows.append(sub)
+    rows.append(-sub)
+    x = torch.stack(rows).to(dtype)
+    # Random 16-bit words as bf16: about 1 in 256 is NaN, most rows hold one or more.
+    words = torch.randint(0, 1 << 16, (64, extent), dtype=torch.int32).to(torch.int16).view(torch.bfloat16)
+    return torch.cat([x, words.to(dtype)]).cuda()
